fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Circular Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Open Terrain; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Steep Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the road entrance to the driveway so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective posts on both sides to define the opening, particularly given the surrounding dense vegetation.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive to maintain a clear path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back tree limbs overhanging the access drive to maintain vertical clearance for fire and rescue apparatus.
• Keep the access drive surface clear of debris, fallen branches, and loose material that could slow or stop emergency vehicles on the steep grade.
• Post property and driveway length information at the road entrance so responding units know what to expect before committing vehicles.
• Identify and mark a designated turnaround area near the main residence so drivers of large vehicles can reverse direction without becoming stuck.
• Keep the area around the detached structure clear of vegetation that would block vehicle access or movement around the building.
• If a gate exists at the driveway entrance, install a Knox Box or provide a combination to the local fire department so responders are not delayed at the entry point.
• Confirm with your local fire department that the access drive can support the weight of a fully loaded fire apparatus given the steep terrain and drive length.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Mixed Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Long Driveway; Single Access Route; Grass Cover; Limited Vegetation Separation; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim trees and shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the structure.
• Thin the tree clusters nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove or cut back shrubs growing within the scattered shrub areas closest to the house.
• Mow or cut the grass cover around the structure regularly, especially during dry months.
• Separate the mixed vegetation areas near the structure by removing the plants closest to the building.
• Thin trees and shrubs along the full length of the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep overhanging branches trimmed back from both sides of the driveway to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back any vegetation that narrows the driveway or blocks sightlines along its length.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from within the scattered shrub areas near the structure.
• Thin shrubs and small trees in areas where vegetation grows in dense, connected patches leading toward the structure.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding the structure as clear of low-growing vegetation as practical.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible from the road for emergency responders using the single access route.
